content:
About a year ago, Jony Ive and Sam Altman previewed a brand-new concept AI hardware product, making grand promises at the time.

The latest reports suggest OpenAI may technically deliver on that promise, but it could end up competing to some extent with an upcoming AirPods model. If so, it's easy to imagine AirPods Ultra being the more popular choice...

OpenAI 硬件裝置嘅承諾

The two previewed their AI hardware device in a video released last May. The video was frustratingly sparse on the device's form factor details, but they did claim this product was something completely new.

「I think this is going to be the coolest piece of technology that the world has ever seen.」 「So at a minimum, something that should be thought of beyond these legacy products.」 「I am absolutely certain that we are on the verge of a new generation of technology that can make us our better selves.」

As I said at the time, you can't make those kinds of promises and then come out with a product category we've already seen.

配備鏡頭同感應器嘅智能喇叭

A smart speaker is absolutely one type of smart hardware product we've seen before. However, the latest reports suggest that's exactly what we should be expecting now. Bloomberg says the difference is the inclusion of a camera and other sensors.

Whether this really represents an entirely new category of technology is certainly debatable, but it's hard to deny that a device like this could be far more capable than existing smart speakers.

但可能會同 AirPods Ultra 形成某程度嘅競爭

However, this combination—a device you can talk to, with a camera so it knows what's happening around you—isn't actually new. Our iPhones can already do this with Visual Intelligence. Meta smart glasses and competitors' models can too. That sounds a lot like what we're expecting from the upcoming AirPods Ultra.

Of course, speakers and earbuds don't compete directly, but there's use case overlap. Smart speakers are more convenient to use at home than wearing something on your ears, and multiple people can use them. But OpenAI has specifically talked about a device you'd carry with you, and I'll say, for use outside the home, AirPods obviously look like a much more convenient form factor.

Maybe there will be a surprise, but as things stand, I can't imagine carrying a portable speaker around with me every day, except for a few situations where I'd already do that, like going away for the weekend and wanting to listen to high-quality music in a hotel room or vacation rental. Contrary to what the promo video suggested, I can't think of any scenario that would have me taking it to a bar.

For me, AirPods Ultra seem to have more potential than a smarter speaker. What do you think? Please vote in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments section.
